rv.q: This extraordinarily imaginative, quietly beautiful, and suddenly devastating new play is now performing off-Broadway at Vineyard Theatre in a co-production with National Black Theatre, and in association with the New Group.

Bowl EP is explosively kinetic–two of its three characters spend much of the play on skateboards and the third feels like an perpetual motion machine–but grounds that high energy with a deadpan sense of humor and an unresolved but genuinely sweet relationship between its two skaters...
This set, at once bare-bones and yet complex in a way unlike anything else on stage right now, is only the jumping-off point for Nazareth Hassan’s intriguing new play.
But this is nonetheless a riveting, inventive new work, and a powerful announcement of a new talent in Hassan.
Hassan has managed to raise the strident, repetitive street rhythms and language of rap into an art form that gets to the heart of what ails these three colorful figures.

But about half-way through the play’s 85 minutes, the proceedings take a bizarre turn and what started off as a moving love story of two alienated outsiders reaching out to each other through their love of rap and skateboarding turns into a confusing jumble.
Bowl EP is a work of startling originality, but with underlying humanism that adds depth to the surface outrageousness.

The acting troupe is the draw here, with the least interesting aspect being that they are Asian American, since they are all so well cast and no mention is made of their race in Jack Cummings III's likeable production.
Bowl EP — which really should be called Bowl LP — is an uneven but ultimately rewarding foray into love and performance, about facing one's demons.

cn.t: Critics praise Nazareth Hassan's "Bowl EP" as an extraordinarily imaginative and inventive theatrical experience that defies traditional categorization, blending concert, sporting event, and trippy fantasia with infectious energy and quiet beauty.

vr.q: I liked this show a lot more in retrospect once I was able to form some sort of interpretation, but it was a bit of a hard watch in the moment.
